The Accountant is responsible for maintaining the accuracy and integrity of the brand-wise general ledger and holds overall responsibility for the brand-wise Profit & Loss (P&L), including its preparation, review, and analysis. The role assist with the annual budgeting and periodic forecasting process, monitors actual performance against budget and prior year, and highlights key variances and improvement areas to management.
q: Bachelor's degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.

Minimum of 3–5 years of progressive accounting experience, with a strong background in the F&B or hospitality sector, ideally within a multi-outlet or multi-brand restaurant group in the UAE or wider GCC.

Proven track record of managing month-end and year-end closing within tight deadlines, including journals, accruals, prepayments, and provisions, while maintaining GL integrity, along with hands-on experience in preparing brand or outlet-level P&L statements with variance analysis against budget and prior year covering revenue, COGS %, payroll %, and EBITDA.

Practical experience with UAE VAT returns and corporate tax compliance, a sound understanding of IFRS, and experience coordinating with external and internal auditors, preparing audit schedules, and closing audit findings.
Advanced Excel skills (pivot tables, lookups, financial modelling); exposure to Power BI or similar reporting tools is an advantage.
Advanced proficiency in Oracle Micros POS and ERP systems (e.g., NetSuite, SAP, Odoo, Microsoft Dynamics etc).
r: Take overall responsibility for the brand-wise P&L, ensuring revenue, cost of goods sold, payroll, and operating overheads are accurately recorded, classified, and reported each month.
Prepare monthly P&L reports with variance analysis against budget and prior year, explaining key movements in revenue, COGS %, payroll %, and EBITDA.

Manage the month-end and year-end closing process for assigned brands within agreed timelines, including preparation and review of journal entries, accruals, prepayments, and provisions, ensuring costs are correctly allocated to outlets, brands, and cost centres, including central overheads, rent, utilities, and shared services.

Prepare and review balance sheet reconciliations, including bank, credit card, aggregator, inventory, fixed assets, intercompany, payables, and receivables, ensuring all balances are supported and aged items are cleared.
Review food and beverage cost reports and stock counts with the operations and purchasing teams, investigating unusual variances in COGS, wastage, and inventory.
Assist in the preparation of the annual brand-wise budget and periodic forecasts in coordination with operations and the Finance Director, including revenue, cost, and headcount assumptions.
Monitor actual spend against approved budgets, flag overruns early, and recommend corrective actions to protect margins.
Prepare management reports, KPI dashboards, and ad-hoc analysis for the Finance Director and owners, including outlet profitability, payback, and cost-saving reviews.
Work with outlet and brand managers to review P&L performance, identify cost-saving opportunities, and drive profitability improvements.
Implement and monitor internal financial controls to safeguard the company's assets and ensure the integrity of the GL, recommending improvements to the Finance Director where gaps are identified.
Ensure compliance with local regulations and company policies on payment processing, petty cash, expense claims, and financial reporting.
Prepare and review UAE VAT returns and supporting schedules, and support corporate tax compliance, ensuring timely filing and accurate tax treatment of transactions.
Coordinate with external and internal auditors, preparing audit schedules and supporting documentation and following up on audit findings to closure.
Ensure transactions are processed in line with the approved Delegation of Authority (DOA), and that supporting documents and approvals are properly maintained.
Review supplier invoices, payment runs, and vendor master changes to prevent duplicate, unauthorised, or fraudulent payments.
Supervise, train, and mentor junior accountants and accounts assistants, reviewing their work for accuracy and supporting their professional development.
Maintain and update accounting procedures and process documentation and support continuous improvement of finance processes and ERP usage.

Role Summary: The primary role of the Customs Clearance Specialist is you will manage the customs documentation and compliance processes for international shipments. You will coordinate with customs authorities, carriers, and other parties to ensure timely clearance of goods, minimizing delays and ensuring all necessary paperwork is properly completed. You will also stay updated on customs regulations and trade laws to ensure the business remains compliant with local and international trade rules.
q: Bachelor’s degree preferably in logistics and supply chain management
Minimum 4 years of Customs Clearance or Cross Border experience required.
Experience in or exposure to logistics and ecommerce, preferred.
Work well under pressure in a fast-paced and professional environment.
Flexibility and willingness to do physical work and rotational shifts
r: Customs Documentation: Prepare and process all customs documentation, including import/export declarations, commercial invoices, bills of lading, certificates of origin, and other relevant paperwork.
Compliance: Ensure compliance with all applicable customs laws, regulations, and trade agreements, as well as company policies.
Customs Clearance Process: Submit customs declarations to customs authorities and ensure timely clearance of goods to avoid delays or fines.
Liaison with Customs Authorities: Act as the primary point of contact between customs authorities, shipping companies, and the company to resolve any customs issues or discrepancies.
Tariff Classification & Duties: Calculate and verify customs duties, tariffs, and taxes, ensuring accuracy and minimizing costs.
Record Keeping: Maintain accurate and up-to-date records of all customs documents and transactions.
Problem Resolution: Address and resolve any issues or delays related to customs clearance, including working with customs brokers or third-party service providers.
Consultation & Advice: Provide guidance to internal teams or clients regarding import/export regulations, classification of goods, and documentation requirements.
Risk Management: Identify potential risks in the customs clearance process, such as non-compliance or delays, and take proactive measures to mitigate these risks.
